01

Zone Roles — Push vs Magnet vs Entry

Every active zone on every timeframe plays exactly one role at any given moment. The role is not intrinsic to the zone — it is determined by the zone's position relative to the current structural bias at its own TF and the TFs above it. The same zone can flip from magnet to push zone when a BOS event fires through it.

Push Zone push

Drives price away from it. This is the zone that just fired a BOS event. The H1 supply that caused a bearish eBOS is pushing price downward. It's not something you trade toward — it's the engine behind the current move.

Push zones sit behind price in the direction of movement. They are the most recently confirmed structural zones — the ones that created the current leg.

Magnet Zone magnet

Pulls price toward it. This is an unbroken zone sitting ahead of price in the direction of the push. The H4 demand below current price while D bias is bearish is a magnet.

Magnets sit ahead of price in the push direction. They are the targets — where the current leg is heading. Breaker blocks and HTF counter-zones are the strongest magnets.

Entry Area entry

Entry areas exist only where a push zone and a magnet zone overlap at different TF levels. An entry is the intersection point where the HTF push is active (driving direction), the meso-TF magnet has been reached (price arrived at the correction/reversal zone), and the LTF confirms the turn (M1 CHoCH in the push direction).

Without all three — push confirmation + magnet reached + LTF trigger — there is no entry.

Zone Role Assignment Rules

Zone Position Relative to Bias Role Example
Behind price, caused the last BOS With-trend push H4 supply above price after bearish H4 BOS
Ahead of price, unbroken Against-trend (absorbs push) magnet H4 demand below price during bearish H4 impulse
Ahead of price, beyond last broken HTF level Terminal counter-zone magnet (terminal) H4 demand below broken D LL
Broken zone, polarity flipped Breaker — new direction target magnet (breaker) Former H4 supply, now bullish breaker support
HTF zone where LTF CHoCH fires Nested confirmation entry M1 CHoCH inside H1 supply at H4 push zone
02

The TF Cascade — How D Pulls H4, H4 Pushes H1

The TF cascade is the directional engine. Each timeframe layer sets the context for the layer below it. Macro defines direction. Meso defines the leg. Micro defines the entry. Skipping a layer (going from D bias straight to M1 triggers) is the diagnosed root cause of too many false signals.

D bias → H4 zones → H1 legs → M15 sub-waves → M5 / M1 trigger

Layer 1: D Zones Set the Magnets for H4

Example: D Bearish Bias

Push: The last D supply zone (caused the D bearish BOS) sits above price, driving everything down. Every H4 rally that fails to body-close above this D supply confirms it as the active push.

Primary magnet: The nearest unbroken D demand zone below price. H4 is being pulled toward this.

Terminal magnet: The H4 counter-zone — H4 demand sitting below a broken D LL. When price reaches this, the D impulse is exhausted.

Example: D Bullish Bias

Push: The last D demand zone (caused the D bullish BOS) sits below price, driving everything up.

Primary magnet: The nearest unbroken D supply zone above price.

Terminal magnet: The H4 counter-zone — H4 supply sitting above a broken D HH.

Layer 2: H4 Zones Push H1 Legs

Within the D-level directional context, each H4 BOS event pushes a new H1 leg. The H1 zones that form during this leg inherit the directional context — but their role depends on where they sit.

H1 Zone Position Inside H4 Context Role What Happens at This Zone
H1 demand, mid-impulse H4 zones 1–5 correction magnet Price touches, H1 HL fires, push resumes
H1 demand, late impulse H4 zone 6–7 exhaustion magnet Price touches, bounce weaker, nearing terminal
H1 demand at H4 counter-zone H4 zone 8 + counter-zone terminal magnet H1 HL fires = FLIP preparation
H1 supply (correction peak) H1 LH at H4 push zone entry area M15→M5→M1 CHoCH here = with-trend entry
Full cycle: Bearish BOS continuation (LL→BOS→LL→BOS) → terminal LL → CHoCH (first HH) → bullish BOS continuation. The supply/demand zones at reversal points show where push zones flip to magnets and vice versa.

Layer 3: How H1 Legs Create Entry Areas

The entry area is where the H1 correction leg ends and the push leg resumes. It sits at the intersection of the H4 push zone (above, in a bearish context) and the H1 LH supply zone that forms during the correction:

D bearish push  →  sets H4 magnet below
  H4 bearish BOS  →  pushes H1 impulse leg down
    H1 impulse completes  →  H1 correction leg up begins
      H1 LH forms at / near H4 push supply  →  ← THIS IS THE ENTRY AREA
        M15 LH inside H1 supply
          M5 LH inside M15
            M1 CHoCH (LH) = ENTRY TRIGGER
03

Multi-TF State Machine — Reading All Layers

At any moment, the mechanical state is a tuple of five TF layers. Each layer is a fact — derived from zone events, not discretion. The combination determines the context mode and whether an entry exists.

Layer State Variables Determines
D (Macro) Bias (bull/bear/neutral) · Last event (HH/HL/LH/LL) · Distance push→magnet Overall direction, which side to trade
H4 (Meso-Macro) Bias · Zone count in impulse · Counter-zone proximity · Last event Exhaustion clock, terminal detection
H1 (Meso) Phase (impulse/correction) · Zone count · Position vs H4 zones Leg phase — the missing meso layer
M15/M5 (Micro) Sub-wave position within H1 leg · CHoCH direction Timing, H1 leg completion signal
M1 (Execution) CHoCH event at HTF zone Entry trigger — only fires when all above confirm

Context Mode Mapping

RIDE — With Trend

State: D + H4 aligned · H4 zones 1–5 · H1 correction completing

Action: Enter at H1 LH/HL zone when M1 CHoCH fires in push direction

Push: H4 supply/demand behind price

Magnet: Next H1 zone in push direction

FLIP — Terminal Reversal

State: H4 zone 8 + at H4 counter-zone · H1 CHoCH fires opposing direction

Action: Enter at H1 demand/supply after H1 BOS confirms reversal

Push: Flipping — old push zone becoming magnet

Magnet: Breaker block from previous push

SCALP — Hedge (Counter-Trend)

State: H1 BOS fires (sweep) · Retracement to H1 zone

Action: M1 CHoCH at H1 zone = scalp entry · Rides H1 correction leg

Target: Next H1 zone in correction direction

SKIP — No Trade

State: D and H4 not aligned · Or H4 zones 7–8 without counter-zone confirmation · Or H1 phase unclear

Action: Wait. No signal until layers re-align.

Orderflow shift: Bearish orderflow (LL→LH→LL→LH) shifting to bullish via CHoCH (HL breaks the LH pattern), then BOS confirms with HH. The CHoCH is the early signal — the BOS is the confirmation. This is how H1 CHoCH creates H4 structure.
CHoCH reversal (left) vs BOS continuation (right): Left panel shows bearish→bullish CHoCH with supply/demand zones marking the reversal. Right panel shows bullish trend with ascending demand zones — BOS continuation. The push zones (demand in uptrend, supply in downtrend) are behind price. The magnets (opposing zones) are ahead.

04

Reversal Areas — Terminal Exhaustion

Reversal areas are not discretionary — they are defined by three converging mechanical signals. All three must be present for a terminal reversal to be valid.

The Three Convergence Signals

Signal 1: Zone Count Terminal

H1 impulse has produced 5+ unbroken zones in the push direction, plus a correction sequence of up to 3 zones. Zone 8 reached = terminal. This is the exhaustion clock.

Signal 2: H4 Counter-Zone Reached

Price is inside the H4 demand (bearish impulse) or H4 supply (bullish impulse) that sits beyond the last broken D structural level. This is the H4 counter-zone — the terminal magnet.

Signal 3: LTF Structural Shift

H1 CHoCH fires in the opposing direction (first HL in bearish impulse, first LH in bullish impulse). Followed by H1 BOS confirming the new direction. The breaker from the previous push becomes the target.

Terminal Bottom Sequence (Bearish → Bullish Reversal)

H1 zone count hits terminal (5 impulse + 3 correction = zone 8)
  ↓
Price enters H4 counter-zone (H4 demand below broken D LL)
  ↓
H1 HL fires — first CHoCH — correction starting
  ↓
H1 HH fires — BOS — reversal confirmed in new direction
  ↓
Breaker from H4 supply (drove the move down) = upside magnet
  ↓
Persisted H4 zone (captured at original H4 eBOS) = intermediate target
  ↓
M15 HL inside H1 demand → M5 HL → M1 HL inside M5 supply = ENTRY

Terminal Top Sequence (Bullish → Bearish Reversal)

H1 zone count hits terminal (5 impulse + 3 correction = zone 8)
  ↓
Price enters H4 counter-zone (H4 supply above broken D HH)
  ↓
H1 LH fires — first CHoCH — correction starting
  ↓
H1 LL fires — BOS — reversal confirmed
  ↓
Breaker from H4 demand (drove the move up) = downside magnet
  ↓
M15 LH inside H1 supply → M5 LH → M1 LH inside M5 demand = ENTRY
Valid vs invalid BOS/CHoCH (Gold H1): Green checks mark valid structural breaks. Red X marks show premature or invalid BOS calls. POI H1 zones mark the areas where price reacted. $$$ marks liquidity sweeps. The distinction between valid and invalid depends on whether the zone count and HTF context supported the break.

Entry Mechanics — The Full Cascade

Every entry follows the same three-layer template. No exceptions, no shortcuts. Skipping a layer produces false signals.

1. MACRO confirms direction    →  D bias + H4 zone count = context mode
2. MESO confirms leg phase     →  H1 impulse/correction + position vs H4 zones
3. MICRO confirms timing       →  M15 CHoCH inside H1 zone → M5 → M1 CHoCH = trigger

RIDE Short Entry (With-Trend)

Conditions: D Bearish · H4 Zones 1–5 · H1 Correction Completing
StepEventWhat It Confirms
1 H1 completes correction up (H1 HL → H1 LH forms) H1 LH supply = correction peak reached
2 H1 LH supply overlaps with / near H4 push supply Meso confirms: correction into push zone
3 M15 makes LH inside H1 supply Sub-wave turning — M15 structure shifting bearish
4 M5 makes LH inside last M15 demand Precision — nested confirmation tightening
5 M1 CHoCH (LH) inside last M5 demand ENTRY

Stop: Above H1 LH supply top

Target: Next H1 demand below (the next correction magnet)

FLIP Long Entry (Terminal Reversal)

Conditions: H4 Zone 8 at Counter-Zone · H1 CHoCH + BOS Confirmed
StepEventWhat It Confirms
1 H1 HL fires (CHoCH) at H4 counter-zone Terminal exhaustion — first reversal signal
2 H1 HH fires (BOS) — reversal confirmed New trend direction validated
3 M15 HL inside H1 demand that just formed Sub-wave confirms pullback into H1 demand
4 M5 HL inside last M15 supply Nested confirmation
5 M1 CHoCH (HL) inside last M5 supply ENTRY

Stop: Below H1 demand bottom (inside H4 counter-zone)

Target: Breaker block from previous H4 push supply

SCALP Hedge Entry (Counter-Trend)

Conditions: H1 BOS Fires (Sweep) · Price Retraces to H1 Zone
StepEventWhat It Confirms
1 H1 BOS fires (sweep event) — impulse leg completes Liquidity taken, impulse exhausted short-term
2 Price retraces to H1 zone (demand/supply from BOS leg) Correction reaching institutional zone
3 M1 CHoCH at H1 zone SCALP ENTRY — rides H1 correction

Exit: At next H1 zone in correction direction

Early Confirmation Cascade — CHoCH Propagation

An H1 CHoCH doesn't just confirm an H1 event — it IS the mechanism that creates H4 structure. Every HTF structural shift is built from LTF CHoCH events cascading upward.

M1 CHoCH → M5 direction → M15 leg complete → H1 sub-wave → H4 structure → D structure
HTF EventConfirmed Early ByEarliest Tradeable Signal
H4 HH H1 HH (supply top > prev H4 supply top) M1 HL after H1 first HL
H4 LL H1 LL (demand bot < prev H4 demand bot) M1 LH after H1 first LH
H4 HL H1 HL sequence inside H4 demand M15 HL inside H1 demand @ H4 demand
H4 LH H1 LH sequence inside H4 supply M15 LH inside H1 supply @ H4 supply
D LH H4 HH capped below D supply top H1 CHoCH (first LH after H4 HH)
D HL H4 LL floored above D demand bot H1 CHoCH (first HL after H4 LL)
H1 leg complete M15 CHoCH (opposing direction inside H1 zone) M1 CHoCH after M5 CHoCH inside M15
06

Exit + Re-Entry — Leg Transitions

Exit and re-entry are not separate systems — they are two halves of the same cycle. Every exit creates the setup for the next entry. The zone that completes one leg becomes the push/magnet for the next.

Exit Signals (Current Leg Ends)

SignalMeaningAction
M15 correction TL break inside H1 leg H1 sub-wave completing, leg losing momentum Tighten stop or partial exit
M15 CHoCH in opposing direction inside H1 zone H1 sub-wave done — correction or reversal starting Exit at M15 signal
Price body-closes inside breaker zone Breaker retested — target reached Full exit — magnet consumed
H1 zone count reaches 5 (impulse) + correction TL break H1 impulse exhausting, correction imminent Exit and wait for correction completion

Re-Entry Signals (Next Leg Begins)

SignalWhere It FiresEntry
H1 correction completes (H1 LH for bearish, H1 HL for bullish) At H1 correction extreme — new H1 supply/demand zone M1 CHoCH at the new H1 LH/HL zone
Breaker from completed leg forms At the broken zone that flipped polarity M1 CHoCH at breaker = re-entry in push direction
H1 BOS fires in push direction (new leg confirmed) After correction ends, new impulse begins Already positioned from re-entry, or enter on pullback

The Full Cycle — One Directional Push

H1 BOS (sweep) → ride the impulse leg → target: next H1 demand/supply magnet
  ↓
H1 zone reached → SCALP hedge (M1 CHoCH at H1 zone)
  ↓
H1 correction leg plays out → H1 LH/HL forms
  ↓
EXIT scalp at H1 correction extreme
  ↓
M1 CHoCH at the new H1 LH/HL zone = RE-ENTRY in push direction
  ↓
Next H1 BOS leg begins → REPEAT
  ↓
Until zone count terminal (5+3) + H4 counter-zone → FLIP
The Unified Sweep-Scalp-Growth Chain

H1 BOS (sweep) → scalp hedge retracement to H1 zone → M1 CHoCH at H1 zone = one mechanical cycle. This repeats until the zone count gates the cycle. Zones 1–5 allow Growth entries, zone 6 is last entry, zones 7–8 are hold-only, zone 8 inside H4 counter-zone is terminal (FLIP preparation).

07

Breaker & Mitigation in the Framework

Breakers and mitigation blocks play specific roles in the magnet/push framework. They are not "just zones" — their formation rules determine their persistence and the strength of the expected reaction.

Breaker Block — Strong Magnet

A breaker block forms when an external HH/LL break fires — a child TF body-closes through a parent TF structural zone. The broken zone flips polarity:

OriginalBroken ByBecomes
Supply (sellers)Bullish eBOSBullish breaker (support)
Demand (buyers)Bearish eBOSBearish breaker (resistance)

In the framework: Breakers serve as magnets for the new directional move. The FLIP reversal trade targets the breaker from the previous push. The breaker must persist until retested — removing it prematurely loses both the exit target and the re-entry zone.

Breaker confidence weight: ~2× vs mitigation blocks in the rule engine.

Bearish OB vs breaker: Left — supply zone (OB) with liquidity sweep above. Right — same zone after polarity flip = breaker block acting as resistance on retest.

Mitigation Block — Moderate Magnet

A mitigation block forms from a failure swing — price reverses without a full structural break, no liquidity grab preceded the break. The zone acts as a weaker reaction area:

AspectBreakerMitigation
FormationFull reversal + sweepFailure swing, no sweep
ReactionStrong, high convictionModerate, one retest
PersistenceUntil retestedStandard zone lifecycle
Framework rolePrimary magnet / targetSecondary reference zone
Mitigation block: H→LH pattern where the LH zone becomes a mitigation block (MB). Price returns to it and it acts as support — but only for one retest.
Break determines type: Breaker block requires breaks on BOTH sides (liquidity swept, then structural break). Mitigation block = "immature breaker" — only one side breaks (failure swing). The difference is mechanical: did both levels get swept?
Mitigation block + FVG entry: Failure swing creates mitigation block. When price returns and a Fair Value Gap overlaps the mitigation block, that overlap is a high-confidence entry zone. FVG + mitigation block = stronger than either alone.

Persisted H4 Zones — Pre-eBOS Context

When an H4 eBOS fires, the indicator captures the last unbroken H4 zone of the opposite type. This persisted zone serves as an intermediate magnet — the reversal trade's first target before reaching the breaker.

EventPersisted ZoneRole in Framework
Bearish H4 eBOS Last unbroken H4 supply Shows where sellers were positioned — rally target / resistance
Bullish H4 eBOS Last unbroken H4 demand Shows where buyers were positioned — pullback target / support
